headline_marked: Ukraine's [[PM Yulia Svyrydenko resigns]] after just one year in office
headline: Ukraine's PM Yulia Svyrydenko resigns after just one year in office
summary: The resignation comes amid opposition questions over the purpose of the cabinet reshuffle and concerns over corruption and winter energy security.
details: Ukraine's parliament has accepted the resignation of Prime Minister Yulia Svyrydenko, who served in the role for only one year. The 40-year-old economist stepped down on Tuesday, though President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has not yet named a successor.

Opposition lawmakers have questioned the motives behind the sudden change, noting the lack of clarity regarding the goal of the reshuffle. Some critics argued that Svyrydenko did not take sufficiently strict measures against corruption during her tenure.

In her farewell speech, Svyrydenko emphasized that every day of the year required tough decisions and firm steps. She warned that the incoming government's biggest challenge will be managing the winter, as Russia may intensify attacks on power and gas infrastructure.
Speculation suggests that Serhiy Koretskyi, head of the state-owned oil and gas company Naftogaz, could be the next Prime Minister, with a vote expected in parliament this Thursday.

President Zelenskyy has already met with Koretskyi and Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov. Observers note that if Fedorov is also removed, it would signal a major strategic shift in Kyiv's approach to long-range strike capabilities.

The Ukrainian Prime Minister is primarily responsible for domestic policy, managing the wartime economy, reconstructing infrastructure damaged by Russian strikes, and advancing economic reforms requested by Western donors.
During her term, Svyrydenko's government navigated a difficult winter and managed complex relations with the US administration while beginning technical talks for European Union membership.
caption:
Ukraine's Prime Minister Yulia Svyrydenko has resigned after only one year in office. Who will take over as the country faces a critical winter?

Ukraine's parliament has accepted the resignation of Prime Minister Yulia Svyrydenko, who served in the role for only one year. The 40-year-old economist stepped down on Tuesday, though President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has not yet named a successor.

Opposition lawmakers have questioned the motives behind the sudden change, noting the lack of clarity regarding the goal of the reshuffle. Some critics argued that Svyrydenko did not take sufficiently strict measures against corruption during her tenure.

In her farewell speech, Svyrydenko emphasized that every day of the year required tough decisions and firm steps. She warned that the incoming government's biggest challenge will be managing the winter, as Russia may intensify attacks on power and gas infrastructure.

Speculation suggests that Serhiy Koretskyi, head of the state-owned oil and gas company Naftogaz, could be the next Prime Minister, with a vote expected in parliament this Thursday.

President Zelenskyy has already met with Koretskyi and Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov. Observers note that if Fedorov is also removed, it would signal a major strategic shift in Kyiv's approach to long-range strike capabilities.

The Ukrainian Prime Minister is primarily responsible for domestic policy, managing the wartime economy, reconstructing infrastructure damaged by Russian strikes, and advancing economic reforms requested by Western donors.

During her term, Svyrydenko's government navigated a difficult winter and managed complex relations with the US administration while beginning technical talks for European Union membership.

Source: Prothom Alo
